memory_candidates.content: When extracting a heading-gated section verbatim per mode-gated-section-loading.md, a mechanical 'promote every line matching #+ ' heading-promotion step will ALSO promote fence-interior text that merely looks like a heading (a literal sample-output template, an echoed report format) if it isn't tracking fenced-code-block state. This silently rewrites supposedly-verbatim content and, for an output-format template, misrepresents what the command actually prints. Fix: track ``` fence state during promotion and only touch lines outside a fence. Caught in task 89 (skill-literature/skill-distill mode-gated extraction) via round-trip diff review before committing -- the diff showed extra heading-level changes beyond the expected real-heading promotions, in spans already flagged by the fence-aware boundary scan as containing fence-interior fake headings (## Conversion Complete, ## Literature Validation Report, ## Index Entry Added, ## History/## Connections). General rule: before trusting a heading-promotion script's output on any file with fenced examples, diff its full promoted-body output against the pre-extraction original and confirm every changed line is a real heading at the expected level, not a fence-interior line that drifted past a naive line-prefix match.

A file-level allowlist in a lint keyed on a literal source file PATH (e.g. lint-scoped-commit-boundary.sh's EXCLUDED_FILES array, each entry a path + inline reason) silently stops covering its documented exception the moment that content is relocated by a refactor (a mode-gated-section extraction, a file split/rename) -- the lint then flags previously-exempted, unchanged content as a brand-new violation. When moving content out of a file that carries a path-keyed allowlist/exemption entry anywhere in the repo, grep the destination content for markers that would make it independently identifiable (a distinctive comment, a known pattern) and check whether any OTHER file's allowlist/exemption references the OLD path by name -- then move the entry, don't just leave a now-silently-broken exemption. Caught in task 89 only because the post-move full gate run (verify-deploy.sh) was actually executed before closing the task, not skipped as 'should be fine, it's just a move'.
